findingProjection.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:549-550 hardcodes the literal string proof-or-stop for the bin key lookup instead of reusing the existing CANONICAL_ROOT_PACKAGE_NAME constant (defined at line 117 and already used at lines 1153/1291 for the same command name). Low risk of drift if the bin/command name is ever renamed in one place but not the other.

packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:558-561,613-616 (inspectGlobalCoreExecutable + checkGlobalCoreRealpath) added in this story a distinct warning branch for a global bin target that is missing/not-a-file (executableFacts.binTargetExists=false), which renders a different remediation string ("...does not exist; rebuild: npm --prefix <realpath> run build") than the non-executable-mode branch. CHK-003:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence (packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs cases 4 and 5) only exercises: case 4 = bin target present but mode 0644 (non-executable, file exists), case 5 = .worktrees/ realpath drift with an executable bin. Neither case, nor any other verificationEvidence for CHK-003, constructs a package whose declared bin target file is absent or is a directory, so the ENOENT/non-file sub-branch and its rebuild remediation string are never executed by any test -- grep for rebuild|does not exist across the test file returns zero hits. This is exactly the kind of drift the story is meant to catch (a broken/missing build artifact behind global proof-or-stop), so the untested branch is in-scope, not incidental.

commit b13839b411 (git cherry-pick -x from story/B-83aa 8ebfff3550) modifies packages/main/src/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts and packages/main/src/tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts, neither of which is in .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/scope-contract.json allowedModify/allowedCreate, and no checklist item carries a reason for the scope change. Content verified correct (byte-identical body to 8ebfff3550, cwd-neutrality assertion is non-vacuous, DYNAMIC_BINDING_BUILD_CEILING 808->809 is harmless since B-e256 adds no new .ts source and the guard still reports builds=808), but the story now carries an unreviewed-under-this-story, cross-story commit authored for B-83aa CHK-004 embedded via cherry-pick before B-83aa has landed on main. This is a scope-contract/provenance gap (mode=shadow, so not mechanically blocked), not a functional defect: recommend amending scope-contract/checklist to record the reason, or landing the shared F-023/ceiling fixture fix on main directly instead of duplicating it across in-flight stories via cherry-pick.

packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1576-1587 defaultCompiledCoreVersionProbe (the production probe actually wired by default at line 248) has two branches -- the readFileSync catch (unbuilt/missing dist/core/proof-or-stop-brand.js, ENOENT) and the COMPILED_CORE_VERSION_RE non-match (partially built or unparsable content) -- that are never exercised by any test using the DEFAULT probe. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs case 29 (around lines 950-970) only injects a compiledCoreVersionProbe STUB via extraOptions to simulate a probe failure; writeCorePackage/makeRepoWithWorktree never pass compiledVersion:null (which would skip writing the brand file) or malformed brand-file content, so the real function's own ENOENT and unparsable-content error messages are dead-in-tests. Separately, unlike its sibling BRAND_EXPORT_RE in core/version-bump.ts (which the doc comment at lines 1562-1573 claims this is the same regex shape as), this probe applies COMPILED_CORE_VERSION_RE with no comment-stripping and no duplicate/ambiguous-match guard -- version-bump.ts throws on more than one match (version-bump.ts:213-218) precisely because a second export-shaped occurrence (e.g. in a comment) would let exec() silently pick the wrong one; defaultCompiledCoreVersionProbe has no equivalent check, so a future brand-file comment change that happens to contain export-shaped text would silently report the wrong compiled version rather than failing loudly. Low risk today (no such occurrence exists in the real file) but it is exactly the untested/unguarded shape this round was asked to scrutinize.

packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1576-1587 defaultCompiledCoreVersionProbe (the production probe actually wired by default at line 248) has two branches -- the readFileSync catch (unbuilt/missing dist/core/proof-or-stop-brand.js, ENOENT) and the COMPILED_CORE_VERSION_RE non-match (partially built or unparsable content) -- that are never exercised by any test using the DEFAULT probe. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs case 29 (around lines 950-970) only injects a compiledCoreVersionProbe STUB via extraOptions to simulate a probe failure; writeCorePackage/makeRepoWithWorktree never pass compiledVersion:null (which would skip writing the brand file) or malformed brand-file content, so the real function's own ENOENT and unparsable-content error messages are dead-in-tests. Separately, unlike its sibling BRAND_EXPORT_RE in core/version-bump.ts (which the doc comment at lines 1562-1573 claims this is the same regex shape as), this probe applies COMPILED_CORE_VERSION_RE with no comment-stripping and no duplicate/ambiguous-match guard -- version-bump.ts throws on more than one match (version-bump.ts:213-218) precisely because a second export-shaped occurrence (e.g. in a comment) would let exec() silently pick the wrong one; defaultCompiledCoreVersionProbe has no equivalent check, so a future brand-file comment change that happens to contain export-shaped text would silently report the wrong compiled version rather than failing loudly. Low risk today (no such occurrence exists in the real file) but it is exactly the untested/unguarded shape this round was asked to scrutinize.

Render compiledVersion (or clearly label both manifest and compiled values) and add a stale-compiled-version row assertion. severity: medium

concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:52 fixed-clock waitForFile deletion is incomplete: DESCENDANT_PID_READY_TIMEOUT_MS remains as an unused declaration after every consumer was replaced by lifecycle-bounded waitForChildFile; this dead residue contradicts the new child-lifecycle waiting concept and can mislead future maintenance. severity=critical

quality-runtime-probe-parse: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1566-1568 accepts every non-empty `npm root -g` stdout value as a valid filesystem root, although the new structured-probe contract says unparsable output must be a failure. Verified against the built candidate with PATH resolving `npm` to `/bin/echo`: stdout `root -g` produced globalCoreRealpath.status=pass, installed=false, and npmRoot=`root -g`. A noisy, wrapped, or corrupt npm response is therefore misreported as known absence and defeats the fail-closed doctor diagnostic. severity: medium

quality-bin-target-stat-probe: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-708 catches every statSync failure and reports binTargetExists=false with verification=ok. Verified against the built frozen candidate using an existing executable bin below a mode-000 parent: stat failed with EACCES, but globalCoreRealpath said the target does not exist and prescribed only npm rebuild. This conflates an unreadable or I/O-failed installed target with ENOENT, discards the errno, and can send operators through a rebuild that cannot repair permissions or filesystem access. Preserve non-ENOENT probe failures as unverifiable drift with the errno and add a hermetic denied-stat case. severity: medium

quality-bin-target-containment-prefix: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:98-100 treats every relative path beginning with `..` as outside `dist`. A valid package.json bin target such as `dist/..cli.js` yields `relative(...) === "..cli.js"`, so restoreBinExecutableBits skips it; a targeted probe against the frozen candidate returned restored=[] and left mode 0644. This violates the CHK-001 contract to restore every listed in-dist bin target and can leave the linked CLI non-executable. Use an exact parent traversal check and add a hermetic in-dist dot-prefix case. severity: medium

packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:139,160,203,230,258 only exercise a one-entry object-form package.json bin, while scripts/promote-dist.mjs:93-96 contains a distinct string-shorthand branch and iterates arbitrary object values. Repository search found no test using bin:"dist/cli.js" or two declared bin targets. A regression could leave a shorthand target or one of multiple targets at 0644 while every current selector remains GREEN, contradicting CHK-001 and the plan promise to restore every listed package.json bin target. Add hermetic string-shorthand and multi-target cases that assert every target becomes executable, remains byte-identical, and appears in the restored list. This is distinct from F-010, which covers the in-dist containment prefix boundary. severity: medium

concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts:469,483 deletes the PIN MAINTENANCE guidance block but leaves two live references to the now-nonexistent maintenance note ("the maintenance note above" and "see PIN MAINTENANCE above"). Repository-wide rg confirms no PIN MAINTENANCE block remains, so future validate.commands digest drift points maintainers to instructions that this Story removed; the deletion is incomplete and the residual assertion/comment are misleading. severity=critical

quality-bin-target-type-validation: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:101-103 chmods and records every lexically in-dist target without verifying that statSync(target).isFile(). A targeted frozen-candidate probe declared dist/cli.js as a directory: restoreBinExecutableBits returned ["dist/cli.js"], changed its mode to 0755, and the target remained a directory. promoteDist therefore accepts and promotes a malformed staging tree while reporting the bin target restored even though the global CLI target is not an executable file. packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs covers absent targets and stat/chmod failures but has no non-regular-target case. Reject non-regular bin targets before promotion and add a hermetic directory case. severity: medium

quality-smoke-descendant-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:312-338 and 405-425 kill only the direct CLI child on the harness ceiling or wait bound, then fail without cleaning the command descendants; the alive-descendant assertion also has no cleanup when it detects the regression. A bounded process-tree probe matching this parent-only SIGKILL behavior verified that the parent closed while its sleep descendant remained alive. Because descendantTreeCommand launches sleep 600 for the command, idle, and max rows, the exact failure paths this smoke is meant to diagnose can leave orphan processes running for up to ten minutes and contaminate later validation. Retain a process-group or descendant cleanup handle and terminate/reap it in a finally path before failing. severity: medium

quality-smoke-platform-regression: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:352-357 hard-codes /bin/sh and the external sleep utility for every new descendantTreeCommand row, replacing the prior process.execPath-based child fixture. proof-or-stop.config.json registers this smoke as an unconditional validation command, while the validation implementation and validation-tier planner explicitly model native win32 execution. On native Windows, spawning /bin/sh fails with ENOENT before the descendant PID can be published, so the command, idle, and max deadline assertions cannot exercise their subject and escalated/full validation fails for host reasons. Use process.execPath with a platform-neutral inline descendant fixture, or provide an explicit win32 branch with equivalent process-tree semantics. severity: medium
